messages:
alex: Heads up — the latest npm release (v1.3.0) broke the JS quickstart sample and a few customer apps. Getting runtime errors about imports and missing dist files.

maria: Ugh. Any error logs?

alex: Repro: npm i @redwood/inference@1.3.0 then node ./examples/basic/server.js -> 
Error: Cannot find module './dist/index.cjs'
Also in browser/edge builds we see "Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'" when importing the package.

sam: Sounds like package.json is pointing to the wrong entrypoints. Could be missing both .cjs and .mjs outputs or exports map is wrong for edge targets.

jordan: Our publish job printed a warning about no "dist" folder being included in the tarball but the job still succeeded. CI logs: 
ci-bot: [publish] created package @redwood/inference@1.3.0 (files: package.json, README.md, src/, types/) — note: dist/ not found

maria: That explains it. We accidentally published src/ instead of compiled output. That'll break both node CJS and ESM consumers plus edge runtimes that require .mjs.

sam: Also check package.json fields: "main" should point to cjs entry, "module" or "exports" map for ESM, and "types" to the d.ts in dist. If we only ship TS sources then types links are wrong too.

ajex (typo, actually alex): repro in Vercel Edge: import inference from '@redwood/inference' -> SyntaxError because file has `export` from TS -> transpilation not applied. Edge expects ESM .mjs.

jordan: Minimal quick fix: republish a patch that includes compiled artifacts (cjs + mjs), set package.json exports: 
{
  "main": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "module": "./dist/index.mjs",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
    }
  }
}

maria: We should also include source maps: dist/index.cjs.map and dist/index.mjs.map and update package.json "files" to include dist and source maps so customers can debug.

sam: Agreed. Also add a prepublish check in CI: verify dist exists and exports resolve for both node and browser/edge. I can add a script that runs node -e "require.resolve('@redwood/inference')" and a tiny esbuild bundle targeting edge to ensure ESM entrypoint works.

alex: Who can cut the patch? We need to revert the broken release or publish 1.3.1 ASAP. Customers hit this in a deploy.

jordan: I'll yank 1.3.0 from npm (unpublish or deprecate) and push a hotfix branch with compiled artifacts. Will need a fast review.

devrel: Heads up — customer-facing sample apps in the docs site are down. I'll update quickstart README with a temporary workaround: "use @redwood/inference@1.2.5 or pin to 1.2.x" until patch is out.

sam: I'll open a PR with: build -> dist (cjs + mjs), types emitted, proper exports map, include source maps, and CI checks. Tagging @maria for review.

maria: Thanks. Also add a changelog entry explaining the packaging fix and mention edge compatibility notes (must ship compiled .mjs for edge runtimes).

alex: For follow-up: add a release checklist to prevent publishing without compiled outputs, and add an automated smoke test that runs on npm pack contents.

devrel: I'll notify downstream SDK integrators and post an announcement in #general once 1.3.1 is out. :thumbsup:

sam: PR opened -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 (fix: publish compiled outputs + exports map + CI smoke tests). Please review quickly.
_meta: Generated Slack thread about ESM/CJS publishing mistake and source map/build artifact issues
